fixes.explanation: The messenger does tell him about his sons, friend, and I think that news is heavy too. He says, “Your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, are both dead, and the ark of God has been captured.” But the verse points to a different moment: “As soon as the ark of God was mentioned, Eli fell backward from his chair…”

The city gate is where Eli was sitting, friend, but the verse doesn't send her there. She is Eli's daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas. It says that when she heard the news, “…she collapsed and gave birth, for her labor pains overtook her.”

You've got it, baker. The elders say, “Let us bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD from Shiloh, so that it may go with us to save us from the hand of our enemies.” The ark is to come from Shiloh and go with them. So the plan is to haul it out to the battle.

Yes, baker. The verse says all the Israelites raised such a great shout that the ground shook. I've been in a crowd so loud I felt it in my feet, but I've never felt the ground itself shake. That's a LOT of shouting.

That's the word, baker. When they realized the ark of the LORD had entered the camp, the Philistines were afraid. They cry out, “The gods have entered their camp!” They also say, “Woe to us, for nothing like this has happened before.”
Glad doesn't fit, friend. The text says the Philistines were afraid. They say, “Woe to us…” more than once.
The Amorites aren't the ones the Philistines bring up, friend. They say, “These are the gods who struck the Egyptians with all kinds of plagues in the wilderness.” It's the Egyptians they name.
The Moabites aren't in this speech, friend. The Philistines say, “These are the gods who struck the Egyptians with all kinds of plagues in the wilderness.” That's the people they name.
That's what they say, baker. “Take courage and be men, O Philistines!” and then, “Now be men and fight!” They're afraid, and they tell each other to fight anyway.

Reasonable guess, friend, but that's not the word in the verse. It says Eli was sitting beside the road, watching, because his heart trembled for the ark of God. The ark is what his heart is trembling for.
